title: Adoption Pipeline for Serving Economies: Playbook and Rollout for Adaptive Batching, Smart Prefetch, and Quant Profiles
creator: Priya Nair
description: Create a repeatable adoption pipeline and internal playbook that helps product and platform teams safely enable adaptive batching, prefix/KV prefetch (smart prefetch), and targeted quantization profiles. Deliverables: an adoption checklist, gating criteria, rollout templates (canary/A-B/fallback), observability dashboards and per-route cost baselines, and a partner program for early adopter customers.
okrs: O1: Reduce hosted per-token serving cost by 22% across targeted routes by end of Q2 2026
KR1.1: 60% of high-volume routes have adaptive batching enabled with <5% p90 latency regression
KR1.2: Smart prefetch reduces repeat-prefix token compute for 40% of conversational sessions
KR1.3: Safe quant profiles adopted on 30% of eligible models with measured quality delta <1.5% (task-specific evals)
milestones: 2025-12-08 - Console rollout templates and dashboard mockups reviewed with Console PMs
2026-01-12 - Internal alpha: ENG + two product teams enable adaptive batching on staging
2026-02-01 - Smart prefetch prototype validated on reranking workload (10% token savings)
2026-02-20 - Quant profile safety matrix and eval harness integrated into CI
2026-03-10 - Beta: four customer routes running full pipeline with canary control group
metrics: Baseline median per-1k-token cost: $0.21 (hosted catalog avg)
Target median per-1k-token cost after pipeline: $0.164 (-22%)
Latency target: p90 increase <= 5% for routes that enable batching
Quality target: end-to-end task accuracy drop <= 1.5% from quantization
Adoption target: 30% eligible routes in production by 2026-06-30
updates: 2025-11-04: Kickoff sync with Serving runtime, Console, and Applied ML teams. Agreed ownership: Eng runtime owns batching infra, Console owns rollout templates, Applied ML owns quant safety tests.
2025-11-19: Design review - simplified rollout UI accepted; minor UX ask to expose per-route quality regression window.

2026-01-20: Alpha results: two product teams saw avg token savings 12% with adaptive batching; p95 latency unchanged; one route saw spike in tail latency due to bursty request patterns - mitigation planned.
2026-02-05: Smart prefetch reduced KV-cache misses on a conversational test corpus by 18%; need to tighten cache eviction policy to avoid memory pressure on dedicated nodes.

2026-02-22: Quant profiles passed automated evals for search/rerank models; open question: can we automate rollback on classification regressions? Engineering to add model-level rollback hooks (ENG-4210).
2026-02-28: Beta rollout scheduled. Customer onboarding doc and playbook finalized. Preparing post-beta retrospective metrics pipeline.
risks: Quality regressions from quantization on low-resource tasks — mitigated by per-model eval harness and canary windows.
Increased tail latency when batching interacts with bursty traffic — mitigation: dynamic batch timeouts and route-level rate-limits.
Operational complexity for customers on Dedicated/private deployments — mitigate by providing an opinionated default profile and one-click rollback in Console.
Memory pressure from smart prefetch on small GPU nodes — require minimum node sizing or prefetch throttles.
decisions: Use a three-stage rollout: internal alpha -> partner beta -> open beta with guardrails.
Adaptive batching defaults will prioritize latency SLOs; teams can opt in for aggressive batching via route settings.
Quant profiles will be grouped as 'safe', 'experimental' with automated evaluation gates before 'safe' graduation.
